entries.what_happened: Manuscript 'Hilbert's tenth problem over the rational numbers' (main.tex, dated October 6, 2026) claims Theorem thm:main: no algorithm, given f in Z[X_1,...,X_n] with n part of the input, decides whether f has a zero in Q^n. The proof builds, for nonconstant f, a computable sequence of finite rational-solvability tests such that f has an integer zero if and only if every test succeeds. Its ingredients are a rank-one elliptic curve over F = Q(sqrt 2) supplying integer indices (Proposition ell:rank), a five-point height estimate (Theorem hei:height), a pole-parity positive existential formula obtained from two-descent (Proposition par:pole-parity), and prime-pattern lemmas. Corollary thm:degree-normal-form adds that the rational problem has Turing degree 0', and that the same holds for integer polynomials of total degree at most four and for sums of squares of degree at most two, with no bound on the number of variables. The other manuscript, 'A pointwise 2-converse for elliptic curves with rational two-torsion', is not about Hilbert's tenth problem; the Hilbert manuscript cites its Theorem 1.1 as an input (see conditional_on).
entries.delivers: Settles the case K = Q, negatively: solvability over Q of integer polynomials is undecidable, with the number of variables part of the input. Field reading (K is the field the unknowns range over): K = Q is the open rational case, and this is the one case of the bullet the manuscript decides. Ring reading (solvability in the ring of integers O_K): K = Q is Matiyasevich's 1970 theorem, so nothing new there. The manuscripts make no claim about any other number field K, either as a field or through its ring of integers. The proof is over Q; Q(sqrt 2) appears only as an auxiliary field for the elliptic curve. The introduction cites results for other K (Koymans and Pagano 2026, and Alpoge, Bhargava, Ho and Shnidman 2026, for the ring of integers of every number field; Poonen; Mazur and Rubin, conditionally) as background, not as claims of this family. So the manuscripts do not identify a class of number fields, and do not claim to answer the bullet as worded.
entries.remains: Field reading: for every number field K other than Q, whether solvability over K itself is undecidable; the manuscripts neither say which K are undecidable nor say that their method extends. Ring reading: for every K other than Q, nothing in these manuscripts. The manuscripts also state that their restricted corollaries are Turing-equivalent results, not many-one completeness, and that the construction gives no single existential definition of Z in Q.
entries.direction: proves undecidability for K = Q only (negative answer over the rational field); no class of number fields
entries.conditional_on: (i) The pole-parity step (Section 03, Lemma par:global-point) uses Theorem 1.1 of the pointwise 2-converse manuscript to get finiteness of Sha(E_l/Q) for curves E_l with full rational two-torsion and 2^infinity-Selmer corank at most one. The Cassels-Tate pairing argument is written out in the text. (ii) The modularity step of the height estimate (Section 04) uses the odd regular Fontaine-Mazur theorem at 2, cited as Theorem 1.1 of the OpenAI preprint 'Fontaine-Mazur modularity at the prime 2' (October 6, 2026). That preprint is outside this family and I did not read it; the text states that its hypotheses are verified for the representation at hand. (iii) The prime-pattern lemma (Section 06) uses the Green-Tao-Ziegler inverse theorem, cited with a 2024 erratum that the text says leaves the stated inverse theorem unchanged. (iv) Other cited published results include Faltings, Bost, Zarhin, von Kaenel and Kret, Silverman, and Davis-Putnam-Robinson-Matiyasevich.
entries.doubts: The text flags no step as sketched and contains no hedge about the main theorem. The abstract and Theorem thm:main agree. The main limits are the ones the text itself states: the restricted corollaries are Turing-degree statements only, and the construction gives no bound on the number of variables and no single existential definition of Z in Q. The argument is written in an elementary-extension and compactness style, with transfer principles used in the key divisibility and height steps. Its dependence on the 2-converse manuscript and on the Fontaine-Mazur preprint is as described above. I checked the statements and the main assembly, not every proof step.

entries.what_happened: Manuscript 'A pointwise 2-converse for elliptic curves with rational two-torsion' (paper.tex, dated October 7, 2026) claims Theorem 1.1 (thm:main): for E/Q with E(Q)[2] nonzero and s_2(E) = corank over Z_2 of Sel_{2^infinity}(E/Q) equal to 0 or 1, ord_{s=1} L(E,s) = rank_Z E(Q) = s_2(E), and Sha(E/Q) is finite. The method builds integral interpolation families of quadratic twists, using cyclotomic classes (Kato), Heegner and ring-class deformations, and finite prime networks, and recovers the value or derivative at the given curve. For analytic order 0 or 1 the manuscript uses the published Gross-Zagier and Kolyvagin theorems to pass from analytic order to rank and finiteness of Sha. The introduction says the broader companion 'Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse' (cited as OpenAIGoldfeldTwoConverse2026) is not an input to this proof. The Hilbert manuscript in this family does not bear on BSD.
entries.delivers: For the subclass of curves with nonzero rational two-torsion and s_2 at most one, the theorem gives: (1) the rank part, ord_{s=1} L(E,s) = rank E(Q), since both equal s_2; and (3) finiteness of Sha(E/Q). It covers CM and non-CM curves, every rational isogeny configuration, and every reduction type at 2 and at the bad primes, as the text says. Since s_2 is at least the rank, this subclass has algebraic rank at most one; the new content is the direction from Selmer corank to analytic order, while the direction from analytic order at most one to rank is Gross-Zagier-Kolyvagin. Part (2), the leading-coefficient formula, is not addressed: the text says it 'does not assert the full Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer leading-coefficient formula'. The matching pass's summary ('Selmer corank at most one gives equal analytic and Mordell-Weil rank and finite Sha') leaves out the hypothesis E(Q)[2] nonzero, which the theorem requires. The bullet asks about every elliptic curve over Q; the manuscript does not claim that.
entries.remains: (a) Curves over Q with no rational two-torsion point, for parts (1) and (3). (b) Curves with s_2 at least 2; this includes every curve of algebraic rank at least 2, since rank is at most s_2. (c) Part (2), the leading-coefficient formula, for every curve, including the subclass: the Tamagawa product, the regulator, the order of Sha and the torsion order are not shown to match the leading Taylor coefficient. (d) For the subclass, part (3) is proved, but the leading-term formula in (2) still needs (c).
entries.direction: proves the rank equality and finiteness of Sha for a subclass (rational two-torsion, Selmer corank at most one); leading term not addressed
entries.doubts: The text flags no step as sketched. The argument is long (about 7,000 lines of TeX over nine sections), and I read the introduction, the main-theorem assembly and selected hypotheses, not the full proof. Some propositions carry hypotheses that the text later says are discharged. In coefficients.tex the odd-source lower bound is introduced with 'assume for now', and the text says the coefficient calculus 'is conditional on these lower bounds; it does not establish them'; Proposition pw:odd-lower is said to supply them. In ring-determinants.tex, Proposition rd:assembly adds an assumption on generic cohomology for the binary data, and the proof of rd:missing-vertex says that assumption is verified. ring-limits.tex omits two fields with extra units and the CM field when choosing companions. I did not verify these discharges.
